items.alt_text: Box plots of foreign countries visited by 20-year-olds show Germans visited the most, Americans next, and Chinese the fewest.
items.long_description:
Figure 2.44 is three horizontal box-and-whisker plots sharing one horizontal axis, one plot for each country. The horizontal axis shows number of foreign countries visited in a lifetime, ranging from 0 to 11 with a mark and label at each integer from 0 to 11. The countries are listed vertically from top to bottom: China, Germany, and United States.

China (top): a single horizontal line with short vertical caps at each end spans from about 0 on the left to about 5 on the right. No box is drawn and no median line is drawn, so the first quartile, median, and third quartile are not visible as separate drawn parts; the drawn minimum is about 0 and the drawn maximum is about 5.

Germany (middle): a left whisker line with a cap at about 0 extends to the left edge of a box at about 4. The box extends to about 8. The right edge of the box is dashed, which is the median line sitting on the edge of the box, indicating the median at about 8 coincident with the third quartile. A right whisker line extends from the dashed edge at about 8 to a cap at about 11. So the drawn parts are minimum about 0, first quartile about 4, median about 8, third quartile about 8 at the same dashed edge, and maximum about 11.

United States (bottom): a box extends from about 0 on the left to about 5 on the right. Inside the box a dashed vertical line marks the median at about 2. No separate left whisker extends beyond the box, so the left edge of the box at about 0 is both the minimum and the first quartile. A right whisker line extends from the right edge of the box at about 5 to a cap at about 11. So the drawn parts are minimum about 0, first quartile about 0 at the left edge of the box, median about 2, third quartile about 5 at the right edge of the box, and maximum about 11.

Overall pattern: Chinese 20-year-olds report the lowest and narrowest range, about 0 to 5, with no visible spread of quartiles. German 20-year-olds report higher values, with the middle half of the data between about 4 and 8 and the median at the top of that interval near 8. United States 20-year-olds are intermediate and right-skewed, with the bottom quarter at about 0, half at or below about 2, and the upper half spreading from about 5 to about 11.
